title: The first L²-Betti number of aspherical manifolds and Poincaré duality groups of dimension at least three
subject: math.GT
abstract: The L²-Betti numbers b_p⁽²⁾ of a finite complex measure the square-summable harmonic p-chains on its universal cover. Singer's conjecture says that for a closed aspherical manifold of dimension n, one whose universal cover is contractible, they vanish outside the middle degree n/2. A manuscript of OpenAI dated 25 September 2026, released on 6 October 2026, proves the conjecture in dimension four; it is not refereed. Its proof assumes b₁⁽²⁾ > 0, builds from functions of finite energy on the fundamental group Γ a compact boundary on which Γ acts, and reaches a contradiction; dimension four enters only in a preliminary section. We show that the same argument gives b₁⁽²⁾ = b_{n−1}⁽²⁾ = 0 for every finite aspherical Poincaré complex of formal dimension n ≥ 3, hence for every closed aspherical topological manifold of dimension at least three (Theorem A), and for every finitely presented Poincaré duality group of dimension n ≥ 3 (Theorem B). To do so we state what Sections 3-10 of the manuscript prove as a criterion for groups (Theorem C): a finitely presented torsion-free group with one end, with H²(Γ; F₂Γ) = 0 and with no splitting over a finite or two-ended subgroup, has b₁⁽²⁾ = 0; and we prove, in every dimension n ≥ 3, the facts about Γ that the criterion needs. Theorems A and B depend on the manuscript's argument, which we cite and do not reproduce. One AI referee has followed that argument line by line and found no fault; no human has checked it, or this paper.
comments:
Theorem A: for every finite aspherical Poincaré complex of formal dimension n >= 3, hence for every closed aspherical topological manifold of dimension n >= 3, the L2-Betti numbers b_1 and b_{n-1} vanish. Theorem B: the same for finitely presented Poincaré duality groups of dimension n >= 3. Theorem C is the group criterion that Sections 3-10 of OpenAI's manuscript 'The Singer conjecture in dimension four' (dated 25 September 2026, released 6 October 2026, unrefereed) prove when read for their hypotheses: a finitely presented torsion-free one-ended group with H^2(G; F_2 G) = 0 and no splitting over a finite or two-ended subgroup has b_1 = 0. We cite that argument and do not reproduce it; Section 3 says where it calls on dimension four and lists its 38 statements with their inputs. New here are the reductions of Section 2 in every dimension n >= 3 and for PD(n) groups, with full proofs. That the method gives every n >= 3 was observed, without proof, by u/Apprehensive_Sand951 on r/math in October 2026. Theorems A and B rest on the unrefereed argument and should be cited with that condition.

Checks: Section 2 by Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.2, and an independent check of the finished text; Sections 3-10 of the manuscript read line by line by Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max, Sections 8-9 again by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort high. No human has checked it; nothing is formalized. Records: https://github.com/KokunoYumeto/mathematics-workbenches
